claims.text: Conventional metal parts, including steel components, are used in hot-dip aluminum plating equipment.
Conventional metal parts are susceptible to corrosion by molten aluminum.
A stabilized alumina coating can be applied to pre-made metal components by thermal spraying or plasma processing.
Hot-dip aluminum plating exposes equipment components to molten aluminum at approximately 660 °C.
The proposed processing will produce a dense alumina layer.
The proposed alumina layer will adhere well to the underlying metal.
Alumina is chemically inert toward molten aluminum under the proposed operating conditions.
Alumina has a high melting point and adequate thermal stability for exposure to molten aluminum at approximately 660 °C.
The alumina coating exhibits low wettability with molten aluminum.
A dense, adherent, and poorly wetted alumina layer will act as a physical and chemical barrier between molten aluminum and the metal substrate.
The barrier will inhibit reactions between molten aluminum and the underlying metal.
Alumina-coated components will have lower corrosion and erosion rates in molten aluminum than uncoated components.
The reduction in corrosion and erosion will extend component service life.
Uncoated conventional metal components undergo significant corrosion and erosion during high-temperature contact with molten aluminum.
Coating defects, poor adhesion, or thermal-expansion mismatch with the substrate can diminish the coating's protective capability.
The magnitude of corrosion-rate reduction and service-life extension remains to be established experimentally.
